scope: Saved PC-side evidence, independent host-only decode and public primary-document research. No console, disk, ATA or TRIM command was issued.

exact_device.capture_context: Historical Windows11 smartctl7.5 SAT/USB-to-ATA acquisition, October13 and14. The old PC disk numbers are not current device selectors.
exact_device.proof_level: runtime-observed PC device advertisement; statically decoded saved report; not PS3 transport observation

capability_findings.finding: The exact saved Lexar advertises ordinary DSM/TRIM and up to8 descriptor blocks of512B per DSM command.

capability_findings.evidence: word69=0x4d20: bit14=1 and bit5=1; smartctl JSON trim.supported/deterministic/zeroed alltrue
capability_findings.finding: The drive advertises deterministic read-after-TRIM and zeroed data. No discard was executed or read back in PERF001.
capability_findings.limits: Not a filesystem-zero guarantee across PS3 encryption; not proof every requested LBA was trimmed, host forwarding, OS issuance, timing, usefulness or safety.

capability_findings.evidence: word76=0x850e bit8=1; word75=0x001f => maxdevice depth32; word77=0x0006 bit6=0
capability_findings.finding: NCQ is advertised, but SEND/RECEIVE FPDMA QUEUED is not advertised. NCQ support alone does not establish queued DSM/TRIM.
capability_findings.PS3_use_or_effective_queue_depth: unknown; a synchronous application loop does not prove the entire driver has depth1

capability_findings.finding: LBA48 is advertised. User-sector count is4000797360, maximumuserLBA4000797359, capacity2048408248320B. It exceeds28-bit addressing and stays below2^32 sectors.
capability_findings.limits: Not proof of PS3 high-LBA placement or correct forwarding of every extent; native capacity qualification remains separate.

capability_findings.finding: Device advertises1.5/3/6Gb/s; saved PC capture reports current6Gb/s. Exact console negotiated signal rate remains unknown from these captures.
DMA advertised; MWDMA0..2 and UDMA0..6 advertised; PC report selectsUDMA6. This legacy transfer-mode field is not the PS3 SATA signal rate or a measured throughput ceiling.

capability_findings.evidence: word83 bits12/13=1; word84=0x4163 bit6=1; word87=0x4163 bit6=1
capability_findings.finding: FLUSH CACHE, FLUSH CACHE EXT, WRITE DMA FUA EXT and WRITE MULTIPLE FUA EXT are advertised. PS3 issuance and completion/durability chain remain unknown.
capability_findings.limits: word84bit7=0 is obsolete in ACS-3/4, despite legacy Microsoft WriteQueuedFua field; it does not settle contemporary NCQ-FUA. Do not bypass or change cache/flush behavior.

capability_findings.feature: Volatile cache, read look-ahead and SMART
capability_findings.finding: Volatile write cache supported (82:5=1) but disabled in saved PC capture(85:5=0). Read look-ahead and SMART supported/enabled(82/85:6 and:0=1).
capability_findings.limits: Historical PC cache state cannot be transferred to current PS3 state. A volatile ATA cache capability is not identification of DRAM, pseudo-SLC cache, or power-loss protection.

capability_findings.finding: ATA Power Management advertised; APM/EPC/HIPM/DIPM not advertised in selected fields; DIPM not enabled in PC capture.
capability_findings.limits: Both HIPM and DIPM bits beingclear conflicts with the ACS-3 expectation that at leastone is supported; report the bits rather than invent support or conformance. PS3 behavior remainsunknown; no settings changes proposed.

capability_findings.finding: Advertised logical512B and one logical per physical sector=>512B physical. Words117..118 lengthfield is not applicable.209 offsetbits are0 but209 is not applicable under word106:13=0.
capability_findings.limits: Does not identify NAND program/erase geometry, partitionalignment, filesystemextent alignment, encryption-unit boundaries or4KiB read-modify-write amplification.

primary_sources.title: T13/2161-D ATA/ATAPI Command Set-3, Revision5
primary_sources.primary_authority: T13 draft specification; full document mirrored by Harvard course site. Despite URL filename, title page is ACS-3 Revision5, not ATA8-ACS.
primary_sources.proof_level: primary normative draft; generic command and IDENTIFY semantics; exact Lexar advertises ACS-4
sections: 7.5, printedpp81..83(PDFpp104..106): DSM06h,48-bit,DMA,TRIM bit and ranges; Table33 read semantics; partial ranges may be trimmed before command-aborted error
7.10..7.11, printedpp101..102(PDFpp124..125): FLUSH CACHE/E7h and FLUSH CACHE EXT/EAh
7.43.4, printedp224:SFQ DSM requires SEND/RECEIVE queued and logsupport
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: IDENTIFY fields distinguish support, enabled state, sector counts/geometry and SATA/queue capability. DSM carries host LBA ranges; deterministic/zero read semantics depend on advertised bits. A command-aborted DSM can already have trimmed ranges, so an error is not proof nothing changed. Flush completion waits for nonvolatile-media persistence or error. These generic definitions do not demonstrate PS3 issuance or forwarding.

primary_sources.title: Microsoft IDENTIFY_DEVICE_DATA structure(ata.h)
primary_sources.proof_level: primary SDK structure documentation; corroborating field layout, not PS3 implementation or normative conformance proof
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: The ATA IDENTIFY structure maps DSM/TRIM, deterministic and zero-after-TRIM, SATA/NCQ, LBA48, flush/FUA, cache, DMA and logical/physical fields. Legacy field names require specification-version checks, especially obsolete queued-FUA bits.

primary_sources.title: smartmontools RELEASE_7_5 ataprint.cpp
primary_sources.proof_level: primary implementation of saved report decoder
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: smartctl7.5 generates supported/deterministic/zeroed from169bit0,69bit14 and69bit5, matching the independent saved-word decode. It reports advertisement rather than executing TRIM.

primary_sources.title: smartmontools RELEASE_7_5 ataidentify.cpp
primary_sources.proof_level: primary decoder metadata; corroboration, not device behavior
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: Versioned decoder labels distinguish current-signaling and device capabilities and identify several historical bits as obsolete. The saved compact report does not provide a full raw-sector checksum witness.

primary_sources.title: The importance of Garbage Collection and TRIM processes for SSD performance
primary_sources.proof_level: primary SSD-manufacturer generic mechanism explanation; no exact-Lexar evidence
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: NAND programming and erasing use different granularities. GC copies still-valid pages before erasing blocks; host discard informs the drive which LBAs are no longer needed. Filesystem deletion alone does not necessarily convey this information. Background/idle GC is controller-dependent.

primary_sources.title: Understanding SSD Over-provisioning(OP)
sections: Maintaining Performance and Endurance via Over-Provisioning(OP)
primary_sources.proof_level: primary manufacturer explanation plus Kingston-specific examples; no Lexar sizing or outcome evidence
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: Controller-reserved non-user capacity supplies workspace for GC/wear management and can improve sustained/random writes. OS free bytes, host-unused LBAs, factory spare capacity and already-erased NAND are different quantities. Kingston's enterprise examples do not quantify this Lexar.

primary_sources.title: Samsung V-NAND SSD870QVO Data Sheet Revision1.1
sections: p4:Optimal Performance for Everyday Computing Experience
primary_sources.proof_level: primary manufacturer example for a different SSD; not installed-Lexar evidence
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: Advertised870QVO sequential-write performance uses Intelligent TurboWrite. The sheet separately specifies80MB/s(1TB) and160MB/s(2/4/8TB) after TurboWrite and differentiatesQD1/QD32. TRIM requiresOS support. This demonstrates why cache state and queue depth need controls; none of these controller/NAND/cache numbers apply to the Lexar.

primary_sources.title: Lexar NQ1002.5-inch SATA III SSD product page
primary_sources.proof_level: primary product-family marketing/specification; no serial/FW-revision characterization
primary_sources.short_paraphrase: NQ100 family includes2TB SATA6Gb/s and advertises up-to550MB/s reads; write rates are lower and actual performance varies. Product performance may vary by shippingdate/inventory. The inspected page does not identify the installed SN21128 controller, NAND, DRAM, SLC cache size or sustained-write floor.

additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.title: Linux v6.16 arch/powerpc/include/asm/lv1call.h
sections: LV1_CALL definitions: storage_read, storage_write, storage_send_device_command, storage_get_async_status, storage_check_async_status
additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.proof_level: primary Linux/OtherOS ABI definition; corroborate against exact saved CEX callsites before binding names
additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.short_paraphrase: Storage ABI IDs are read245(6inputs,1output),write246(6,1),send-device-command248(6,1),get-async-status249(1,2),check-async-status254(2,1). OtherOS declarations do not prove current CEX forwarding or filters.

additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.title: Linux v6.16 drivers/block/ps3disk.c
additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.proof_level: primary Sony-authored Linux/OtherOS storage driver; not installed GameOS driver
additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.short_paraphrase: OtherOS uses a64KiB bounce buffer and a single-request tag set. READ/WRITE use LV1 sector calls; flush uses LV1 device-command0x23(HDDOUT). IDENTIFY uses device-command2 with an ATA taskfile. Request dispatch has READ/WRITE/FLUSH and a rejecting default, without discard. These are documentary Linux constraints, not measured or static CEX constraints.

additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.title: Linux v6.16 drivers/ps3/ps3stor_lib.c
additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.proof_level: primary Sony-authored Linux/OtherOS library; not runtime evidence on current console
additional_primary_command_and_OtherOS_r.short_paraphrase: The sector wrapper sends deviceID,regionID,start,count,flags0,LPARbuffer and receives a tag; the command wrapper sends deviceID,command,four arguments and receives a tag. Completion/status are handled separately. DMA setup checks bounce-buffer alignment. This supports ABI interpretation only.
